subject: Intermittent streaming stalls during high-throughput jobs — exec attention requested
content:

Date: Sat, 14 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Intermittent stalls in streaming responses (observed 02:00–05:00 PST)

Olga / Redwood team —

We've hit repeated stalls in the live recommendation pipeline overnight. Customers see the UI spinner hang for ~20–40s, then either a 502 or an incomplete card (missing final chunk). Our engineers captured a few request IDs (attached) that end with a TCP FIN after the last chunk; looks like the client never receives the final terminator. Error aggregation shows an increased streaming error rate of ~4.7% in the 02:00–05:00 PST window, which is affecting revenue flows for our flash sale.

Can you confirm whether this is a platform-side regression? We need a mitigation plan and ETA.

—Liam
Liam O'Connor
Head of Platform Engineering, Acme Retail

Adding context from our telemetry: between 02:00–05:00 PST we saw a pattern of partial chunk delivery on a subset of requests routed to the eu-west-2 pool that had longer average seq lengths. p95 token-latency for streaming segments jumped to ~1.2s and we saw a spike in keepalive-driven connection resets. We also observed a small number of WebSocket idle-timeout disconnects shortly after burst windows.

I pulled a few logs and attached a sample (acme_error_samples.txt). Dylan, can infra confirm whether kernel-level socket buffers or an NLB connection limit could be dropping the final chunk?

—Marissa Cole
VP Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference

From: dylan.brooks@redwood.ai
To: marissa.cole@redwood.ai; olga.petrov@redwood.ai; hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 14 Feb 2026 12:48:00 -08:00
Subject: RE: Intermittent stalls in streaming responses

Quick update from infra investigation:
- We see sustained connection churn at the edge during the 02:00–05:30 window (spikes in SYN_RECV / TIME_WAIT).
- A subset of the problem requests are routed to older serving instances with an older nginx config that had a short chunked transfer flush interval and an aggressive proxy_read_timeout (30s).
- There were also GC pauses on a runner handling long-context requests which delayed final chunk emission; downstream proxies then closed the connection before the final flush.

Immediate mitigation proposed:
1) Hotfix: increase proxy_read_timeout to 90s on the affected layer and bump chunk flush interval to emit smaller intermediate chunks more frequently (reduces chance of a large final chunk being dropped).
2) Roll traffic away from the older instance pool with config drift (can be done in ~25 minutes).
3) Deploy a small runtime patch to ensure final-chunk flush happens on the application thread even during GC (non-disruptive restart of a subset of runners).

Marissa/Olga — Do you want me to execute the hotfix now? This will require an on-call override and an exec notification because this is impacting a paying customer's revenue window.

—Dylan Brooks
Infrastructure Lead, Redwood Inference

From: grace.oconnor@redwood.ai
To: olga.petrov@redwood.ai; marissa.cole@redwood.ai; dylan.brooks@redwood.ai; hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 18 Feb 2026 16:35:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent stalls in streaming responses — exec summary

Team — executive summary for leadership and Acme:

Root cause (current assessment): a combination of three factors that align under high-throughput, long-sequence workloads:
1) Config drift: an older nginx/proxy config in a subset of serving nodes had short proxy_read_timeout and aggressive write-buffer settings.
2) Runtime GC/pressure: a small percentage of long-context runners experienced GC-induced pauses that delayed final-chunk emission.
3) Edge connector limits: under burst loads the edge NLB showed elevated connection churn and occasional truncated TCP handoffs during graceful termination.

Actions taken:
- Immediate hotfix (proxy_read_timeout -> 90s, smaller chunk flush cadence) rolled (02:40 PST) and traffic steered off older pool.
- Runtime patch scheduled and rolled to 30% of runners (non-disruptive) — fully deployed by 18 Feb 03:00 PST.
- Edge team increased NLB ephemeral conn window and added a retry path for final-chunk confirmation.
- Drafted customer-facing postmortem and a short SLA credit proposal (attached).

Current status: error-rate down to ~0.4% for the overall stream traffic; p95 streaming token latency returned to baseline. Acme reports residual surface area on very long-context sessions (<0.1% of requests) where client-side timeouts still trigger; we are working with their SREs to harden client keepalive and retry logic.

Recommended exec asks:
- Approve a one-off SLA credit for Acme (proposal attached).
- Fast-track config drift detection for proxy/nginx settings (infra + product OKR).
- Prioritize a test harness for long-sequence streaming under burst loads (research + infra).

If approved, I'll send the postmortem and credit note to Acme and loop in Sales Ops for the contract change.

—Grace O'Connor
Head of Customer Success (Interim), Redwood Inference
